name: India
summary: India's space programme began in 1962 under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and has grown into a full-spectrum capability spanning launch vehicles, Earth observation, navigation, planetary science, and human spaceflight — including a successful lunar south-pole landing and India's first interplanetary mission reaching Mars orbit on its first attempt.

name: United States
summary: The United States, primarily through NASA alongside a growing commercial sector, has led crewed lunar landings, extensive robotic exploration of every planet in the Solar System, and the operation of the most productive space telescopes in history.

name: Europe
summary: The European Space Agency, a collaboration of 22+ member states, has flown missions to a comet nucleus, mapped a billion stars, and contributed major hardware and expertise to numerous international missions including the ISS and JWST.

name: Japan
summary: JAXA is a global leader in asteroid sample-return missions and has flown ambitious lunar and planetary science missions with a strong focus on precision engineering.

name: China
summary: China's space programme has achieved the first soft landing on the Moon's far side, returned lunar samples, landed a rover on Mars, and built and continuously crewed the Tiangong space station.

name: Canada
summary: Canada's space contributions center on robotics — the Canadarm and Canadarm2 have been essential to the Space Shuttle programme and the International Space Station — alongside Earth observation and astronomy instruments flown on international missions.

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: The UAE Space Agency, founded in 2014, achieved orbit around Mars with its first interplanetary mission and has since pursued lunar exploration and a national astronaut programme.

name: Soviet Union (historical)
summary: The Soviet space programme achieved the first artificial satellite, the first human in orbit, the first uncrewed lunar and Venus landings, and the first space station — a distinct historical programme from the modern Russian Federation's Roscosmos, which was established in 1992 after the Soviet Union's dissolution.

name: Russia (Russian Federation)
summary: Since 1992, Roscosmos has continued crewed spaceflight via the Soyuz programme, operated the Mir and (with international partners) ISS Russian segments, and continued launch vehicle development.

name: International
summary: Many of the most ambitious missions in spaceflight history — the ISS, Cassini-Huygens, BepiColombo, and the James Webb Space Telescope among them — are multi-agency collaborations that no single country could have achieved alone.
